c.number.octal.evidence: base prefix `0` takes the unit colour, digits the number colour (P: number prefixes are unit)

cpp.number.oct.evidence: base prefix `0` takes the unit colour, digits the number colour (P: number prefixes are unit)

py.number.bin.evidence: base prefix `0b` takes the unit colour, digits the number colour

py.number.oct.evidence: base prefix `0o` takes the unit colour, digits the number colour

yaml.folded.evidence: `>` block indicator is keyword-coloured, the `-` chomping indicator qualifier-coloured

yaml.indent.indicator.evidence: `|` block indicator is keyword-coloured, the indentation digit number-coloured

cpp.char.u8.evidence: `u8` prefix takes the string colour, the quote the punctuation colour like every string quote

rs.char.evidence: char literal body takes the string colour, the quotes the punctuation colour like every string quote

cpp.op.compound.bit.evidence: the C++ grammar scopes `|` of `|=` as a bitwise operator and `=` as assignment, so the compound operator is half hazard, half quiet (clangd colours it whole)

py.regex.group.evidence: the regex grammar splits a named group opener `(?P<` into punctuation and a group-name scope

sh.extglob.evidence: the bash grammar does not recognise extglob `@(...)`; `@` is plain text and `(` punctuation

sh.redirect.both.evidence: the bash grammar splits `&>` into a background `&` and a redirect `>`

cpp.op.overload.decl.evidence: clangd marks only the word `operator` as the function; the operator symbols keep the grammar colour

cpp.scope.opover.def.evidence: clangd marks only the word `operator` as the function; the operator symbols keep the grammar colour
